methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Robotics & Manufacturing (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 10 same-sector peers exist in Robotics & Manufacturing, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Amca is a robotics and manufacturing company at the IPO stage, founded by Jai Malik and Eli Giovanetti. The company has raised $76.5M to date. The relevant peer universe comprises 9 comparable companies across robotics and manufacturing—1 public (ticker 277810.KQ) and 8 private firms including Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Generalist AI, and Bedrock Robotics.

The peer-median valuation method is not applicable in this case. While 10 same-sector peers exist within robotics and manufacturing, none meet the filtering criteria for stage alignment, timeline proximity, or valuation-tier similarity required for statistical reliability. Specifically, zero peers qualified as same-stage comparables, zero as adjacent-stage, and zero as similar-tier, falling short of the minimum three-datapoint threshold. A broader all-sector median approach would introduce unacceptable bias given the specialized nature of robotics manufacturing and would not meaningfully inform valuation.

Given the inapplicability of peer-median triangulation, alternative valuation methods—such as DCF analysis, precedent transaction analysis, or qualitative stage-and-capital assessment—would be required to establish a defensible valuation range for Amca's IPO. The primary uncertainty stems from the absence of narrow comparables at Amca's specific maturity and funding level, limiting the precision of market-based benchmarking. Engagement with the public comp and top private peers through direct financial metrics would be necessary to bridge this gap.
